translation_notes: context shim: local httpx.py (httpx is not installed; the region only constructs httpx.Client(follow_redirects=True) and stores it); identical for both sides

context shim: `from loader_context import super` -- the region is a constructor of ProfilesDataset(Dataset); extracted as a module-level function, CPython's zero-argument super() has no __class__ cell, so the name is shadowed by a stand-in that records super().__init__(default_union=True) on the caller's self; identical for both sides
RDF.type -> rdf:type, PROF.Profile -> prof:Profile; RDF and PROF dropped from the rdflib import line on the ldpy side (absorbed by the @prefix declarations)
the mechanical draft declared dcterms/owl/prof/rdf; only prof and rdf are used, so only those two are declared -- DCTERMS/OWL/URIRef stay imported and unused on BOTH sides (extraction artefact)

PYLODE_CONFIG_GRAPH = "urn:graph:pylode-config" left as a Python string: writing it as an IRI island would change its Python type (str -> URIRef) and the region passes it to Graph(identifier=...), so the notation deliberately stops at the module constant
graph.__iadd__(...) and `graph = graph - cbd` left verbatim: explicit rdflib graph algebra, no island applies

negative finding: the two @prefix declarations cost two lines to save two dotted-namespace terms, so the notation is line-for-line neutral-to-negative on a region whose RDF work is graph algebra (cbd, difference, named graphs) rather than triple authoring
